articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; avg 11 published per cycle (57 vs 45 yesterday); 1 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one. Nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Multi-source fell to 28% (16 of 57) from 42% yesterday, just under the 30% target; the jump in volume came mostly from single-source tech and Pakistan economy stories. Dawn supplied 10 of 57 (18%), close to the 20% cap, and seven stories were Pakistan domestic economy and politics. Science recovered to 5 from 0, all from science outlets (New Scientist, STAT, Quanta, Phys.org).
watching: Iran war risk: Israel's army chief resisting a strike, Tehran convening a regional meeting with Saudi and Pakistani officials, and Uzbekistan summoning Iran's ambassador.
Houthis claiming a strike on a Saudi pipeline, and Egypt authorising Saudi defence cooperation.
Brazil after the runoff: Bolsonaro rejecting Lula's win and markets slumping.
Israel's Tuesday vote, the UN finding of extermination in the West Bank, and Hebron expulsions.
Comey charged a third time, and the Fed expected to hold this week.
Uganda quarantining returnees from Congo, and UK sanctions on Sudan commanders over El Fasher.
coverageGaps: Twelve datelines are a country rather than a city (United States ×4, China ×2, India, Brazil, France, Pakistan, United Kingdom, Switzerland), up from six; the missing-dateline metric does not catch them.
Pakistan took seven stories, five of them domestic economy items from Dawn, while Africa had three and Oceania one.
Multi-source dipped to 28%; most tech stories rest on a single outlet.
context: Output rose to 57 across five completed cycles with freshness at a 0.1-day median. The experiment pause holds until 2026-11-05 for the runner cut-over, so the multi-source dip and Dawn's share are recorded for the next round rather than acted on; one day under 30% after a 42% day is not yet a trend.
